tasks.title: Closed issues and their snag pictures are archived into registry/issues-closed.json, automatically at the end of a sherlock run
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from an owner question (does sherlock move closed issues to a side file? No). Independent review applied. Cause class: Capability. issues.py has no archive step: confirmed and wontfix issues stay in <world>/registry/issues.json for good. Measured on southampton-build: issues.json 184 KB, registry/issues/img/ 92 MB (the pictures are the bulk). Prior art: #120 (issues lib and CLI), #152 (hold/unfix, same module). Not the same thing as lib/site/site_archive.py and scripts/site_archive.py, which archive site/ISSUES.txt into site/archive/ISSUES-closed.txt; say so in the new command's help text and docstring. Only issue_log.py and issues.py read issues.json in code; registry_next.py, cell_journal.py and cell_registry.py mention it in comments only; site_pages.py does not read it. DELIVERABLE (a) command and library: 1. `issues.py archive` moves every issue at confirmed or wontfix from issues.json to registry/issues-closed.json, unchanged (ID, snags, fix log, verdicts); fix-landed and open never move. 2. Pictures of moved snags move from issues/img/ to issues/img-closed/ and each snag's image path is rewritten; verify resolves live paths under img and closed paths under img-closed. 3. list, digest and sync read the live file only (digest counts are unaffected by design). show and match also search the closed file; optional list --all. 4. Every mutating command (add snag, verdict, unfix, hold, diagnose, move, merge) finds the issue in either file; anything that sets an archived issue back to open or fix-landed moves it and its pictures back to the live file in the same write. merge and move across files fold the closed issue into the live one (state the rule in the code). 5. Counters next_issue and next_snag stay in the live file only, are never reset, and archive leaves them alone; the closed file carries none. IDs are never reused. 6. Safety: re-read both files right before writing; move picture files first, write the closed file, then the live file, so a crash leaves a duplicate that verify catches, never a loss. verify checks: no ID in both files, no dangling image path in either. 7. Update comment-only mentions in registry_next.py, cell_journal.py, cell_registry.py (no logic change). DELIVERABLE (b) skill and docs text: 8. Sherlock Close the case gets a new step 2, `issues.py archive`, run automatically after verify says OK, then verify again; either failing: report and stop; one report line 'archived N closed issues'; later steps renumber 3-7. The world commit adds only paths that exist among registry/issues.json registry/issues-closed.json registry/issues/img registry/issues/img-closed. Update the sherlock skill's reading line and path list, snag/SKILL.md line 6, rules/process.md line 19, templates/new-world-site/{NOTES,README,ISSUES}.txt and the issues.py docstring. FILES: scripts/issues.py, lib/journal/issue_log.py, lib/journal/test_issue_log.py, .claude/skills/sherlock/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/snag/SKILL.md, rules/process.md, templates/new-world-site/NOTES.txt, README.txt, ISSUES.txt, comment-only in the three registry modules. CHECKS: (a) `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only issue_log` passes with new tests: archive moves confirmed and wontfix only; add snag on a closed issue reopens it and returns its pictures; merge across files; match finds a closed issue; archive everything then add a new issue and a new snag gives higher IDs than before; verify catches an ID in both files and a dangling picture; digest counts are the same before and after. Run these on a temporary world copy, not live Southampton. (b) The owner runs a sherlock close on Southampton once after merge: before and after counts of confirmed plus wontfix issues, `du` of registry/issues/img, `issues.py verify` OK, `show` of an archived issue still prints with its pictures, the commit holds only the world's issue-record paths. Risk: the world checkout is shared with other sessions, hence the re-read before writing.

tasks.title: feature_build --apply refuses a plan that already has a landed build unless told to overwrite
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from an owner observation on west_w34391673. Cause class: Capability. site_kit.apply excludes the plan's own name from the clash check and writes only the new plan's cells, so a re-apply over a landed build leaves old blocks outside the new plan (old roof, stairs, edits). Redo skill now undoes first (e07e331); this is the tool-side guard. feature_build.run: when do_apply and the journal has a landed, not-undone feature entry for spec name, SystemExit pointing at element_undo.py; add --overwrite to opt out. Tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py.

tasks.title: Decor places free-standing hedges the aerial shows (I-035)
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from world issue I-035 (southampton-build): decor hedges come only from the vector map, garden plots and building-border strips, so free-standing aerial hedges never enter the plan. Add decor_plan.aerial_free_hedges: dark-green (shade) columns that are not footprint, canopy or already barriers, grouped into thin elongated strips (>= MIN_BORDER_CELLS long, <= 3 wide); when a lidar heightmap is given, require surface 1-3 above terrain. Resolved hedge items, source aerial, medium confidence; non-strip shade is lawn shade, not a candidate. Wire into build_decor_plan after border hedges. Tests in lib/layers/test_decor_plan.py.

tasks.title: Aerial free-standing hedge detector is off by default (#198 follow-up)
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from a dry run of decor_layer on southampton-build 48,-45. aerial_free_hedges proposed 19 columns, all on carriageway or against buildings (coach and tree shadow), none placeable, and missed the real hedges, which OSM already maps (159 columns) and which are one column wide and flat in lidar. build_decor_plan gains free_hedges=False; the detector runs only when asked. Real cause of lost map hedges beside the bus loop is the layer calling them 'on carriageway' (separate issue). Tests in lib/layers/test_decor_plan.py.

tasks.title: Decor barriers are refused only on carriageway, not on paving, brick or near them
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from a dry run of decor_layer on southampton-build 48,-45: 156 of 159 mapped hedge columns were refused as 'on carriageway', but only 8 neighbouring columns were tarmac; 71 hedge columns stand on live brick/paving and 78 on grass within 2 blocks of paving or brick. Owner decision: the rule should be carriageway only. decor_layer.on_carriageway refuses a barrier column only when its own live ground is tarmac, marking or kerb; the 5x5 near-paving margin and the paving/brick kinds go. Applies to every barrier source. Reason string stays 'on carriageway'. Replaces the #144 brick-path refusal for hedges. Tests in lib/layers/test_decor_layer.py.

tasks.title: Decor uses lidar as a placement and size hint, never as the trigger
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from owner direction after the 48,-45 dry run (201 of 209 unresolved decor items were lone lidar lumps). Rule: a photo, POI, OSM or designer row says there is a feature (statue, wall, hedge, bench, table, anything); decor then consults lidar for placement and size hints. A lump seen only in lidar is ignored: no plan item, not even an unresolved one. decor_plan.lidar_objects stops emitting unlabelled components; a lidar component no longer vetoes OSM/designer furniture unless a photo/aerial label on it names an incompatible kind (e.g. vehicle). Barrier items (map, garden, designer, border) take height from lidar when most columns stand 1-3 above terrain (tree/roof columns excluded); furniture rows carry lidar_height and lidar_cells as hints. Tests in lib/layers/test_decor_plan.py.
